terms.title: Iron Roads
terms.guideSubtitle: A Gothic Western for the Legend Dynamics RPG system
terms.journalIntro: Write it together at the end of a job. Advancements apply to the GM's copies; use each card's Save character file to send a player their update.
terms.journalTitlePlaceholder: e.g. The Harlan County range war
terms.emptyNote: Empty: it won't fire until you reload.
terms.tracksIntro: Shared by all the characters. A killing in the street, a monster seen by townsfolk, or magic worked in the open can mark a box. Lying low between jobs can clear one.
terms.facility: A doctor's surgery with instruments, chloroform and a clean table
terms.formCoreSummary: Monstrous form: changing is a free action; strong emotion can force it (Will roll); its profile applies while changed; townsfolk who see it panic
terms.restrictedToggle: Horror campaign: show vampires as player characters (they must drink human blood; only if the whole table agreed)
terms.restrictedCheck: for horror campaigns only: tick Horror campaign if your table agreed

theme.comment: A gothic ledger by candlelight: slate panels, tarnished-silver rules, blood-red accents, ash falling.

roles.name: Marshal
roles.text: Marshal: carries what authority there is (take a Badge advantage), with Leadership and a steady gun.

roles.name: Deputy
roles.text: Deputy: keeps order, guards prisoners, and backs up the marshal when it comes to shooting.

roles.name: Detective
roles.text: Detective: investigates crimes for the Pinkertons (take Pinkerton Credentials) or a private client, and follows the paper trail nobody else reads.

roles.name: Bounty Hunter
roles.text: Bounty hunter: tracks wanted men across three territories and brings them in, upright or across a saddle.

roles.name: Doctor
roles.text: Doctor: digs out bullets, sets bones, and reads what a body says about how it died.

roles.name: Occultist
roles.text: Occultist: knows the old books, the rituals and the names of things that shouldn't exist, and what each one fears.

roles.name: Lawyer
roles.text: Lawyer: knows the law better than the men who wear the badges, and isn't afraid to say so.

roles.name: Journalist
roles.text: Journalist: asks the questions no one wants asked, and prints the answers.

roles.name: Preacher
roles.text: Preacher: comforts the frightened, counsels the troubled, and stands up to bad men with faith and a shotgun.

roles.name: Gunslinger
roles.text: Gunslinger: the fastest and steadiest gun in the room, and the one who decides when it's time to draw.

roles.name: Scout
roles.text: Scout: finds the trail, reads the land, and keeps everyone alive out in it.

roles.name: Gambler
roles.text: Gambler: reads people, bluffs, and hears everything the saloon hears.

roles.name: Wrangler
roles.text: Wrangler: breaks horses, drives cattle, and can ride anything with four legs.

roles.name: Undertaker
roles.text: Undertaker: buries the dead, and makes sure they stay buried.

skills: Give orders, rally a crowd, keep people together
Calm, train and handle horses, cattle and dogs
Judge motives, spot a lie, read a face
Search a scene, examine clues, follow paper trails
Statutes, warrants, courts, claims and contracts
Monsters, magic, rituals, curses and their weaknesses
Fix and modify guns, locks, machines and traps
Play cards and dice, figure odds, spot a cheat
Follow a trail and read signs of passage
Find water, shelter and food; manage wilderness hazards
Ride, drive a wagon, handle horses in a chase
Climb, swim, jump, run and exert yourself
Move quietly, hide and pick a pocket
formCore: A free action, in or out, except when the moon or the hunger forces it.
Fury, terror or pain can force a change: when it matters, the GM calls for a Will roll.
While changed, your form's attribute bonuses apply to rolls on those attributes and their skills, even above the starting maximum; its traits and drawbacks apply too.
A monstrous form seen by townsfolk marks a box of Whispers.

origins.name: Frontier-born
origins.desc: Raised on a homestead or a ranch, a long way from schools and doctors. Tough, practical, and at home in hard country.
traits: +2 to Survival to read the sky and find shelter before a storm or blizzard hits.
You say what you think, in words townsfolk find rough. Accept the offense it gives at a bad moment.
+2 to Animal Handling to calm, gentle or keep control of a frightened horse.
You don't trust slick talkers and city ways. Accept the cost when your suspicion is wrong.

origins.name: City-bred
origins.desc: Schooled back east or in a western city: you read, you write, you know how the world runs on money and paper. The frontier is still learning you.
traits: +2 to Intellect rolls to recall something from books, newspapers or schooling.
Hard country catches you out. Accept the blister, the lost trail or the laughter when it does.
+2 to Persuasion with bankers, lawyers, officials and the well-to-do.
Your family expects you home, married, or respectable. Accept their letters, visits and pressure.

origins.name: War Veteran
origins.desc: You fought in the war, blue or gray, and came west with what was left of you. You know how to take orders, give them, and keep your head under fire.
traits: +2 to Will against fear when bullets are flying.
The war left more than scars. Accept the nightmares, the shakes or the old wound acting up at a bad time.
+2 to Leadership when organizing armed people to fight or defend.
Men from the other side still hate you, and men from your side still call on you. Accept the grudge or the favor.

origins.name: Drifter
origins.desc: No home, no ties, no questions: you've drifted from town to town for years and learned to read a room on the way in.
traits: +2 to Read People when sizing up a stranger, a saloon or a town on first sight.
You never stay long. Accept leaving when you're needed, or the strain of staying put.
+2 to Stealth when slipping out of a building, a crowd or a town unnoticed.
Someone from one of those towns remembers you. Accept it when they turn up.

origins.name: Immigrant
origins.desc: You crossed an ocean to get here, from Ireland, China, Germany, Italy, Mexico or anywhere else, and you've had to work twice as hard to be treated half as well.
traits: +2 to Persuasion with people of your homeland, and you speak its language fluently.
Some people will never accept you. Accept the slight, the closed door or the threat.
+2 to Body to keep going through long, exhausting labor.
People back home depend on the money you send. Accept the pressure when it runs short.

origins.name: Old Money
origins.desc: Your family has money, land or a name that opens doors. Out here it buys less than it used to, but it still buys plenty.
traits: +2 to Persuasion when money changes hands: bribes, deals and favors bought.
You're used to getting your way. Accept the cost when you don't and won't let it go.
+2 to Leadership or Persuasion with people who know your family's name.
Your family made enemies getting rich. Accept it when they come for you.

origins.name: Railroad Hand
origins.desc: You laid track, drove spikes, fired the engines or blew the tunnels. You know machines, explosives, and how the railroad treats its men.
traits: +2 to Tinkering when setting, timing or defusing dynamite.
You stand with working men against the bosses. Accept the trouble when the company comes down on you.
+2 to Athletics for feats of raw strength: lifting, bending, holding.
Years of dynamite took some of your hearing. Accept it when you miss something said quietly.

origins.name: Sighted
origins.desc: Born with the second sight. You see ghosts, the true faces of monsters wearing human ones, and magic at work. Most people think you strange; monsters think you dangerous.
core: The Sight: when a ghost, a disguised monster or working magic is near, you see it for what it is. Monsters who notice your stare may know what you are.
traits: +2 to Occult to identify a creature and its weakness from what you've seen or what it left behind.
The dead you've seen follow you. Accept the sleepless night or the ghost at a bad moment.
Ability: speak with a ghost that will listen. Roll Will; the dead know only what they knew, and want something in return.
Spirits seek you out. Accept the haunting and its demands.

origins.name: Werewolf
origins.desc: Cursed with the wolf. By day you pass for anyone; under the full moon, or in fury, the beast takes you.
core: Full moon: at moonrise you change, whether you want to or not. A Will roll at −2 delays it a few minutes.
Silver: silver weapons mark one extra box on you and ignore Tough.
The curse: your bite can pass it on, if the GM says so.

traits: Tough: hits of 2+ boxes mark one fewer, except silver
+2 to Tracking by scent, in either form.
When blood is spilled or something runs, the wolf wants it. Roll Will or change and give chase; accept the cost.
+2 to Brawling or Melee against a target an ally attacked this round.
The full moon always comes at the worst time. Accept the changed plans, or the danger to your friends.

origins.name: Dhampir
origins.desc: Child of a vampire and a living mother. You walk in daylight, you heal fast, and the undead fear you, and want you.
core: Undead sense: you feel a vampire or other undead within a short distance, with no details.
Fast healing: rest clears a box every day.
Garlic and holy ground make you queasy: −2 to Will rolls there.
traits: +2 to Melee and Shooting against vampires and other undead.
The blood calls to you. When it's spilled near you, roll Will or feel the hunger take hold; accept the cost.
+2 to Athletics to leap, climb or land safely from a fall.
Your vampire parent wants you back. Accept it when their servants find you.

origins.name: Revenant
origins.desc: You died, and came back for unfinished business. Your heart doesn't beat, your skin is cold, and you won't rest until it's done.
core: Dead flesh: you don't breathe, eat or sleep, and poison and disease don't affect you. Medicine treats you at −2.
Hard to kill: Dying lasts until the end of the next scene, not this one.
Laid to rest: when your business is done, you are too. Agree with the GM what it is.
traits: Your purpose comes first. When it calls, accept the danger or the abandoned plan.
The living sense what you are. Accept the recoil, the dog that won't stop barking, the closed door.

origins.name: Practitioner
origins.desc: A human who works real magic in a tradition: alchemy, witchcraft, the old hermetic arts or worse. Preachers call it devilry, and monster hunters keep a list.
core: Rituals: describe the effect; the GM sets its weight (minor 2, significant 4, major 6 segments); fill that clock with Occult rolls at your tradition's pace.
Charms: carry as many ready charms as your Occult training allows (Trained 2, Specialty 3, Expert 4).
Magic draws attention: working it openly can mark The Dark.
traits: Brews elixirs, poisons and powders ahead of time: hours to make, an instant to use. +2 to Occult when brewing; elixirs keep until the end of the day (a week on success by 5+).
Your craft feeds a vice: greed, drink or worse. Accept it when it bites.
Ritual magic from grimoires, circles and sigils: wards, bindings, divination. An hour per roll, and it needs books. +2 to Occult for wards and bindings.
A grimoire or a secret tempts you beyond sense. Accept the risk to get it.
Curses and hexes worked through a link: blood, hair or a treasured object; −4 without one. +2 to Occult for curses with a link.
People whisper, and the righteous listen. Accept the suspicion, or the mob.
Charms, cards, tokens and folk remedies: small, quick magic. +2 to Occult for charms and fortune-telling.
Your charms demand their rituals. Accept the delay or the odd behavior they require.
Séances and trances that speak with the dead. +2 to Occult to call or question a spirit.
Restless spirits find you. Accept the haunting at a bad moment.
Commands the dead: wake a corpse to answer questions, or to fight for a scene (a minor zombie). +2 to Occult over corpses and the undead.
Your work needs bodies, and people notice. Accept the Heat, the Whispers or the grieving family.
Quick casting along one or two paths agreed with the GM (fire and force, say): one roll per action, and each success fills two segments. You can carry only one charm.
Your power follows one narrow calling. Accept the cost of serving it.

origins.name: Vampire
origins.desc: Undead, ageless and beautiful, with a thirst that never ends. You walk at night and remember centuries. Horror campaigns only.
core: Undead: you don't breathe or age; Medicine can't heal you. Drinking blood can: Will against the victim's Body, and on a success you clear a box and they mark one.
Thirst (horror): each night you must drink human blood, or mark a box that only drinking clears.
Sunlight: 1 box each round in direct sun.
Weaknesses: a wooden stake through the heart incapacitates you; fire and beheading kill; holy symbols give −2 to your actions against their bearer; you can't cross a home's threshold uninvited.

traits: Tough: hits of 2+ boxes mark one fewer, except fire and wooden stakes
drawbacks: Your feral face terrifies everyone who sees it

traits: Ability: meet someone's eyes and roll Presence against their Will; on a success they obey one simple command.
Centuries make enemies. Accept it when one turns up.
Ability: once per scene at night, become mist and escape through any gap.
You won't be slighted by the living. Accept the feud you start.

origins.name: Pact-Bound
origins.desc: You made a bargain with something from below. It gave you power, and it will collect.
core: Infernal power: once per scene, work a minor magical effect with a single Occult roll, no clock. Larger works need rituals.
Hellfire: roll Occult as an attack; a hit marks 2 boxes and sets things alight.
Marked: holy ground, holy water and consecrated silver burn you (1 box).
traits: +2 to Persuasion when making a deal or a promise.
Your patron wants something. Accept the errand, or the price of refusing.
Ability: once per session, ask your patron one question and get a true, unhelpful answer.
Your patron won't share you. Accept it when it interferes with your friends, your faith or your heart.

allegiances: railroad
The Railroad
Once per job, a free ticket, a telegraph message on the company wire, or a word with a division boss.
Duty: the company expects you to protect its interests, even when they aren't right.
baron
A Cattle Baron
Once per job, money, horses or hired hands.
Duty: the baron's range wars become your fights.
army
The Army
Once per job, help from a fort: supplies, an escort or a doctor.
Duty: orders from a commanding officer, and old soldiers' quarrels.
church
The Church
Once per job, shelter, records or a favor from the clergy.
Duty: the Church gives you orders, and its enemies are yours.
gang
An Outlaw Gang
Once per job, a hideout, a fence or a gun at your side.
Duty: the gang calls in favors, and the law knows your face.
order
The Order of the Iron Cross
Once per job, silver, holy water, a hunter's help or the Order's bestiary.
Duty: the Order sends you after monsters, and some of its hunters would count you among them.
coven
A coven
Once per job, a ritual, a remedy or a safe house among witches.
Duty and Vow: the coven's secrets and its quarrels.
reasons: Justice
Somebody has to stand up for the people who can't.
Vengeance
Someone did me wrong, and I mean to settle it.
Fortune
There's money out here for anyone with nerve enough to take it.
A fresh start
Nobody out here knows what I did back east.
Duty
I took an oath, and I keep my word.
Freedom
No boss, no fences, no one to answer to.
Family
Everything I do is for my family.
Faith
The Lord sent me here for a reason, and I believe this is it.
Redemption
I did harm once. I mean to balance the ledger.
Nowhere else to go
These people took me in when no one else would.
connections: Rode together in the war
We served in the same company and still watch each other's backs.
They saved my life
They cut me down from a lynch mob's rope, and I owe them my life.
I saved theirs
I pulled them out of a burning barn, and they haven't forgotten it.
Mentor
They taught me to shoot, ride and survive out here.
Friendly rivals
We're always competing over the same bounty, the same card game or the same sweetheart.
Same hometown
We grew up in the same town and know each other's families.
An unpaid debt
I owe them money, or a favor, and I haven't paid it yet.
A shared secret
We share a secret from a job neither of us talks about.
Saloon regulars
We meet every Saturday night for cards, whiskey and lies.
Bad blood
They blame me for something that went wrong on a past job.
advantages: +2 to Medicine for surgery or digging out a bullet. It does not improve diagnosis.
+2 to Medicine for emergency stabilization of a wounded patient.
+2 to Intellect rolls to notice a concealed physical clue during a deliberate search.
+2 to Shooting on your first shot of a fight, with a holstered revolver.
+2 to Shooting after spending your preceding action aiming at the same visible target.
+2 to Riding in a chase or on dangerous ground.
+2 to Tracking when the trail is more than a day old.
+2 to Gambling at cards, including spotting someone else's cheating.
+2 to Deception to hide what you know or feel under questioning.
+2 to Tinkering when repairing or modifying a firearm.
+2 to Leadership when coordinating others in a sudden emergency.
+2 to Will to resist intimidation, threats or torture.
+2 to Melee with a knife in close quarters.
+2 to Persuasion when calming or rousing a crowd.
+2 to Persuasion when buying, selling or settling a deal.

Legal authority in one town or county: you can carry arms where others can't, question witnesses, make arrests and hold suspects. +2 to Leadership or Persuasion when invoking that authority with people who respect the law. Outside your jurisdiction it's just tin.

Authority across your county: everything a deputy can do, plus serving warrants, running the jail, and swearing in deputies and armed citizens. +2 to Leadership or Persuasion when invoking that authority with people who respect the law.

Federal authority across states and territories: serving federal warrants, pursuing fugitives across county and state lines, swearing in deputies, and calling on local lawmen for help. +2 to Leadership or Persuasion when invoking that authority with people who respect the law.

A commission from the Pinkerton National Detective Agency: carry arms on the job, work a client's case across county and state lines, and draw on the agency's offices and files (records, photographs and descriptions of wanted men). +2 to Investigation when using the agency's records or contacts. You have no powers of arrest beyond any citizen's unless local law deputizes you, and you answer to the client and the agency.
+2 to Occult to identify a creature from what it left behind: tracks, wounds, a body.
+2 to Will against magic, possession and the undead's influence.
complications: A strange discovery tempts you to linger, spend something scarce, or take a risky look. Accept a specific cost.
You shield someone or volunteer for a hazardous rescue at a real cost to yourself.
You won't shoot an unarmed man, break your word, or strike from behind. Accept the setback your code causes.
You insist on arrest, trial and due process. Accept the delay or danger it costs.
Pride tempts you to refuse help or take on too much. Take a real consequence when it matters.
A specific reminder of the war causes hesitation or a hard choice. Define the reminder together.
An agreed secret threatens trust or safety. Earn a point when protecting or revealing it has a real consequence.
A recurring rival complicates your work with concrete problems.
A family or a sweetheart pulls you away from the work.
You've sworn to kill someone. Accept the risk when the chance comes.
You answer insults with fists or guns. Accept the fight you start.
Whiskey or laudanum has a hold on you. Accept the lost night or the slip at a bad time.
Can't Walk Away from a Game
A card game, a bet or a dare is irresistible. Accept the time or money lost.
There's a price on your head somewhere. Accept trouble when lawmen or bounty hunters come.
A debt to dangerous people comes due. Accept their demand.
You seek a way that doesn't end a life. Accept the extra danger.
Something cursed you, and the curse has a will of its own. Agree what it does; accept it when it strikes.
A spirit follows you, and wants something. Accept the haunting and the trouble it brings.
Things that live in the dark know your scent. Accept it when they find you first.

mystery: A strange track or body no one can explain
Everyone's ready to move on, and something is still wrong
An old letter hints at a buried story
protects: A friend is pinned down or hurt
Townsfolk are caught in the crossfire
Someone volunteers for a deadly job in your place
code: The enemy is unarmed or has turned to run
A promise you made becomes dangerous to keep
The easy shot is in someone's back
lawful: A suspect could be shot instead of arrested
The town wants a hanging without a trial
Your friends plan to take the law into their own hands
reputation: Someone questions your nerve in front of others
A job is beyond what you're ready for
Getting help means admitting a mistake
war: Meeting a man who fought on the other side
A field hospital, cannon, or a burning farm
secret: Someone starts asking the wrong questions
Evidence that could expose you turns up
Keeping the secret means lying to a friend
rival: Your rival is after the same quarry
Your rival takes credit for your work
home: The job leads near your family
Someone you love is in danger
vengeance: Word of the one you swore to kill
A face from that day turns up
The chance comes at the worst possible moment
temper: A bully picks on someone weaker
bottle: A long night with nothing to do but wait
wanted: A lawman from back east comes asking
A bounty hunter rides into town
debt: Your creditor wants a favor instead
nonlethal: The man who surrenders is a killer
The only fast solution would kill someone
Your friends vote to shoot first
cursed: The one who cursed you comes back
ghost: A cold room and a familiar voice
Someone the ghost hated comes near
dark: Something has been watching the house

equipment: Six shots; reloading takes an action. Hits mark 2 boxes.
A lever-action repeater with fifteen shots and long range. Hits mark 2 boxes.
Two barrels. Devastating close up (3 boxes and Dying), weak beyond a few paces (1 box).
A tool and a weapon; hits mark 1 box.
Instruments, laudanum, carbolic and bandages. Needed to stabilize a patient and give field treatment.
Gunsmith's and carpenter's tools. Needed for most Tinkering in the field.
Carries you across the territory. Riding in a chase needs one.
Bedroll, canteen, rations, rope and flint for a few days. Turns impossible survival and climbing tasks into ordinary ones.
Light for a few hours. Searching in the dark without light is very difficult (−4) or impossible.
See detail at a distance. Spotting something far off without them is very difficult (−4) or impossible.
Needed to draw up papers, check a statute or argue a point of law away from a courthouse.
Three sticks. Throw with Athletics; the fuse burns for a round. 1 box nearby, 3 and Dying at the centre.
One reload of silver rounds. Silver marks an extra box on werewolves and similar creatures, and ignores their toughness.
Three flasks. Thrown or splashed, it burns undead and demons (1 box) and breaks minor hexes.
A wooden stake through a helpless vampire's heart incapacitates it.
Chalk, candles, herbs, bones and old books. Needed for rituals away from a prepared place.
Held up against undead and demons: −2 to their actions against you, if your faith is real.

tracks.name: Heat
effects: Wanted posters: −2 to Persuasion with lawmen
A warrant and a manhunt: start a Manhunt clock

tracks.name: Whispers
effects: Talk of strange things in the saloon
The preacher names you from the pulpit: −2 to Persuasion with townsfolk
A mob with torches: start a Mob clock

tracks.name: The Dark
effects: Signs and warnings: a marked door, a dead bird

mission: A body found drained of blood
Livestock torn apart in the night
A miner raving about the dead walking
A bounty on a man who died last year
A new preacher packs the church
A town where no one sleeps
place: A logging camp in the deep woods
strange: A werewolf that has acquired the taste
A vampire who owns the town
The dead rising from a flooded graveyard
A witch's curse on a family
A demon summoned by a desperate man
A cult in the church cellar
twist: The law is in on it
A rich man pays for silence
A character's complication comes into play
The monster is protecting its family
The town wants a hanging, any hanging
The Order of the Iron Cross arrives to burn everything
Another hunter is after the same prey
The trail leads to someone a character loves
who: A sheriff who wants it simple
A widow who knows more than she says
A werewolf trying to stay human
A child who saw it happen
A newspaperman who's close to the truth
A dying hunter with a last request

example.name: Josephine Hale
example.role: Detective: investigates crimes for the Pinkertons (take Pinkerton Credentials) or a private client, and follows the paper trail nobody else reads.
example.reason: Somebody has to stand up for the people who can't.
example.connection: Owes the town doctor for keeping quiet about how her last client really died.

comp.trigger: A strange track or body no one can explain

example.contact: A clerk in the Pinkertons' regional office who'll pull a file, quietly

pregens.name: Ruth Calloway
pregens.role: Wears the badge in three counties, and sees what's under the faces of the men she arrests.
pregens.reason: I took an oath, and I keep my word.
pregens.connection: Isaiah Booker brought in the man who killed her father, alive, when he could have collected either way.

comp.trigger: The town wants a hanging without a trial

pregens.name: Dr. Elias Webb
pregens.role: Left a Philadelphia practice for reasons he won't discuss, and patches up whoever comes through the door.
pregens.reason: Nobody out here knows what I did back east.
pregens.connection: Reverend Stone is the only one who knows why he left Philadelphia.
pregens.contact: The editor of the territorial newspaper, who owes him a life

pregens.name: Tom Feeney
pregens.role: Came from County Clare with nothing but a curse, and chains himself in the root cellar every full moon.
pregens.reason: Everything I do is for my family.
pregens.connection: Plays cards with Lucinda Marsh every Saturday, and loses.

pregens.name: Lucinda Marsh
pregens.role: Deals faro by night and reads the cards for anyone who'll pay, and the cards are never wrong.
pregens.reason: There's money out here for anyone with nerve enough to take it.
pregens.connection: Owes Ruth Calloway a favor for a warrant that went missing.
pregens.contact: Mae Lin, a faro dealer who hears everything said at her table

pregens.name: Isaiah Booker
pregens.role: Shot in the back in '69 by the gang he was hunting. He got up again, and he's still hunting them.
pregens.reason: Someone did me wrong, and I mean to settle it.
pregens.connection: Taught Tom Feeney to shoot straight, and still reminds him of it.

comp.trigger: The easy shot is in someone's back

gear.item: A Sharps rifle with a telescopic sight

pregens.name: Rev. Abigail Stone
pregens.role: Gave up a Boston fortune for a circuit of mining camps, and preaches with a shotgun across her knees.
pregens.reason: The Lord sent me here for a reason, and I believe this is it.
pregens.connection: Keeps Dr. Webb's secret, and his whiskey hidden.

comp.trigger: Townsfolk are caught in the crossfire

pregens.contact: Bishop Harrow, who answers her letters and asks no questions

quickRef: Fists, clubs, knives, arrows: 1 box. Guns, heavy blades, claws: 2. Close-range shotgun or buffalo rifle: 3 and Dying.
Derringer 2, revolver 6, shotgun 2, rifle 15. Fan the hammer 3 (−2), both barrels 2 (+2 close), covering fire 3. Reload: one action. Natural 18 jams.
Silver: werewolves. Stake, fire, sunlight, beheading: vampires. Headshot or fire: zombies. Holy water: undead and demons.
Describe the effect; fill a 2-, 4- or 6-segment clock with Occult rolls at your tradition's pace. Charms: Trained 2, Specialty 3, Expert 4.
